Oxidation numbers of Cl atoms marked as \(\mathrm{Cl^a}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^b}\) in \(\mathrm{CaOCl_2}\) (bleaching powder) are

\(\mathrm{Cl^a - Ca - O - Cl^b}\)
_note: The book draws the structure as Ca with a branch to Cl^a and a branch to O-Cl^b. The connectivity is a single chain, so it is written linearly here (Cl^a-Ca-O-Cl^b) with nothing added or lost; no figure crop is needed.

stem: Which of the following is not an example of redox reacton ?
_note: ⚠ Option B is printed with CO2 on BOTH sides — `Fe2O3 + 3CO2 -> 2Fe + 3CO2` — verified at 3x magnification. The standard reaction is Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2, so the reducing agent carbon MONOXIDE has been misprinted as carbon dioxide. Transcribed as printed; an errata bracket is carried on the solution. `reacton` is the book's own spelling in the stem.
solution: [Textbook misprint: option (b) is printed as \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3 + 3CO_2 \longrightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2}\), with carbon DIOXIDE on both sides. The standard reduction of haematite uses carbon MONOXIDE, \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \longrightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2}\), which is a genuine redox reaction (Fe \(+3 \to 0\), C \(+2 \to +4\)); as printed the equation balances neither atoms nor electrons, since iron is reduced with nothing to oxidise. The option is preserved as printed. The answer is unaffected either way: the intended reaction is redox, so option (b) is not the one being asked for, and option (d) — a double displacement in which no oxidation number changes at all — remains the only correct choice.]

stem: A compound contains atoms of three elements A, B and C. If the oxidation state of A is \(+2\), B is \(+5\) and that of C is \(-2\), the compound is possibly represented by

The coefficients p, q, r, s in the reaction

\(\mathrm{p\ Cr_2O_7^{2\ominus} + q\ Fe^{2\oplus} \longrightarrow r\ Cr^{3\oplus} + s\ Fe^{3\oplus} + H_2O}\)

respectively are :
_note: The printed equation carries no H+ on the left, so as written it cannot balance for hydrogen; only the coefficients p, q, r, s are asked for. Transcribed as printed.
